findings.title: Do not skip ownership validation when the Integration is missing
findings.body: The Integration.DoesNotExist branch advances without checking the authenticated GitHub user's relationship to the installation. If the installation webhook has not yet created the local row, a caller can supply another user's installation ID and authenticate with any GitHub account. build_integration then retrieves that installation using app credentials and attaches it to the caller's Sentry organization. This leaves an ownership-check bypass, including a race with webhook delivery. Fail closed when trusted installer information is unavailable, or verify access using the authenticated user's GitHub credentials.

findings.title: Compare immutable GitHub user IDs instead of login names
findings.body: The authorization check compares the current OAuth login name with the historical sender.login stored by the installation webhook. GitHub usernames can be renamed and reused: after the installer changes their username, a different account can acquire the old name and pass this check for an unlinked installation despite having a different identity. The original installer would also be incorrectly rejected. Store and compare the immutable GitHub user ID returned by OAuth against sender.id.

findings.title: Handle integrations without sender metadata
findings.body: This lookup assumes every existing Integration contains metadata['sender']['login'], but build_integration only includes sender when it is present in pipeline state. Integrations created by the successful basic flow, including test_basic_flow, explicitly lack that metadata. If such an integration is later left without an OrganizationIntegration and reconnected, this branch raises KeyError and returns a server error instead of the intended installation-failed response. Handle absent installer metadata explicitly and fail closed or obtain trusted identity information.

findings.title: Preserve coverage of GitHub installation lookup failures
findings.body: The mocked installation endpoint returns 404, but this test now asserts 'Invalid installation request.', which is produced by earlier validation failures. The code handling the actual GitHub 404 still raises 'The GitHub installation could not be found.'. Consequently, the revised test no longer verifies that the installation endpoint is reached or that its 404 is handled correctly. Complete OAuth with valid state, retain the missing-installation assertion, and test invalid OAuth state separately.
